commits.author: James Goldbach
commits.subject: fix(daemon): guard worker PTY null-write + add crash visibility (#223)
commits.body:
Finishes what PR #196 started and adds a visibility layer so future
daemon crashes are attributable, observable, and storm-resistant.

Root cause of the 2026-04-22 restart storm: worker-process.ts:93 had
`injectMessage((data) => this.pty!.write(data), text)` — the same
unguarded non-null-asserted pattern PR #196 fixed at three sites in
agent-process.ts. TypeScript's `!` erases at runtime, so when the
PTY was torn down during inject.ts's 300ms Enter-keystroke setTimeout
window, the callback fired `null.write` → unhandled TypeError →
daemon process crashed → PM2 respawned → discoverAndStart → same
race fired again → 5-iteration storm.

PR #217 (hard-restart IPC) made this latent race start firing
reliably because it actually kills PTYs on hard-restart. Previously
hard-restart was a no-op, so PTY teardown during the inject window
was rare.

Changes:

1. src/daemon/worker-process.ts:93 — one char: `!` → `?.` to match the
   pattern #196 established. Storm root cause fixed.

2. src/pty/inject.ts:83 — wrap the deferred Enter setTimeout callback
   in try/catch. Structural fix: any future caller passing an unsafe
   write callback is now caught. Dropped Enter is logged as warn; the
   daemon stays alive. Covers the whole class beyond just pty.

3. src/daemon/index.ts — add process.on('uncaughtException') and
   process.on('unhandledRejection') handlers. uncaughtException logs
   a FATAL line with full stack, writes .daemon-crashed markers into
   every per-agent state dir, appends to state/.daemon-crash-history.json
   (last 20 crashes, capped), and exits(1) for clean PM2 respawn.
   unhandledRejection records but does not exit (matches Node 15+
   non-strict default). When 3 crashes occur within 15min, a single
   Telegram alert fires to the operator chat (CTX_OPERATOR_CHAT_ID +
   CTX_OPERATOR_BOT_TOKEN env, or falls back to the first agent's .env
   BOT_TOKEN/CHAT_ID). 30-min alert cooldown.

   Debug aid: CTX_DEBUG_ALLOW_CRASH_TRIGGER=1 registers a SIGUSR2
   handler that throws a synthetic uncaughtException — enables live
   verification of the crash-visibility path. Off by default.

4. src/hooks/hook-crash-alert.ts — consume .daemon-crashed marker and
   emit a new `daemon-crashed` end-type variant. Message:
   "🚨 <agent> — daemon crashed, session was interrupted. Resuming."
   Deliberately NOT suppressed during quiet hours (a daemon crash at
   3am historically preceded fleet-wide storms).

5. ecosystem.config.js — document max_restarts: 10 as the intentional
   circuit breaker (fleet goes fully dead after 10 rapid crashes,
   requiring human intervention; storm protection > fleet uptime).
   Add CTX_DEBUG_ALLOW_CRASH_TRIGGER env slot defaulted to '0'.

Tests:
- tests/unit/pty/inject.test.ts — 2 new tests for deferred-callback
  swallow path + normal-path no-warn.
- tests/unit/daemon/crash-handlers.test.ts — 14 new tests covering
  crash-history persistence, crash-loop threshold, 30-min cooldown,
  truncation, window accuracy, marker writing, graceful failure.

Verification (on live fleet, 2026-04-23 ~13:25–13:56 UTC):
- Storm reproduction: spawn-worker + inject-worker + terminate-worker
  within 100ms (exact storm trigger). Pre-fix: guaranteed daemon
  crash. Post-fix: zero errors, daemon uptime grows normally.
- Phase C.1 (single SIGUSR2): daemon exits with FATAL log + full
  stack, 12 .daemon-crashed markers written to state dirs,
  crash-history.json created, PM2 respawns cleanly. Manual hook
  fire emitted "🚨 <agent> — daemon crashed" Telegram.
- Phase C.2 (3 SIGUSR2 in <3min): crash-history accumulates 1→2→3,
  on 3rd crash the operator Telegram alert fires exactly once
  ("🚨 CRITICAL: cortextos daemon is crash-looping ..."), lastAlertAt
  set for cooldown enforcement.
- 11+ hours of passive observation post-deploy: zero new
  TypeError/Cannot-read-properties-of-null errors. Existing ones are
  all from the earlier combined-fixes storm before this PR deployed.

Co-authored-by: Boris <boris@cortextos.ai>
Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: James Goldbach
commits.subject: fix(bus): hard-restart now sends IPC restart-agent to terminate the session (#217)
commits.body:
hard-restart wrote .force-fresh and .restart-planned marker files but never
notified the daemon, so the current session kept running indefinitely.
.force-fresh is only consumed on the NEXT restart — which never came.

Fix: send IPC restart-agent after writing markers, matching the pattern
already used by self-restart. Falls back gracefully when daemon is not running.

Co-authored-by: Boris <boris@cortextos.ai>

commits.author: James Goldbach
commits.subject: fix(daemon): use CronCreate directly on boot to skip /loop cloud-prompt (#210)
commits.body:
The /loop skill calls AskUserQuestion for any interval >=60min, offering
cloud vs. session-only scheduling. During autonomous boot, agents restore
crons from config.json by calling /loop — this blocks the boot sequence
waiting for a user answer that never comes.

Fix: update buildFreshPrompt() and buildContinuePrompt() to tell agents to
call CronCreate directly during boot cron restoration, not /loop. Includes
an inline interval→cron conversion table (6h→"0 */6 * * *" etc.) so agents
can build the cron expression without calling /loop.

/loop is still correct for user-initiated scheduling (mid-session /loop calls
from skills or heartbeats) — this fix is scoped to the boot restore path only.

Also fixes a pre-existing test failure in the comms channels route test:
hardcoded 2026-04-15 timestamps aged past the 7-day archive window; switched
to relative timestamps (2h ago / 1h ago).

Reported by: data agent pipeline audit (docs/pipeline-audit-2026-04-22.md)

Co-authored-by: Boris <boris@cortextos.ai>
Co-authored-by: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: fix(telegram): switch to HTML parse mode — eliminates silent content drops (#181)
commits.body:
* fix(telegram): switch to HTML parse mode to eliminate silent content drops Telegram Markdown v1 silently drops text when it encounters unclosed or unrecognised entities: backtick spans with `--flags`, `$` near numbers, `_` inside filenames, etc. HTML parse mode rejects the whole message with an explicit error instead — no silent data loss. Changes: - sendMessage now converts Markdown to HTML via markdownToHtml(): *bold* → bold `code` → code ```block``` → 
block
_italic_ (word-boundary aware) → italic & < > → HTML entities (always, prevents injection) - Chunking now splits at paragraph/newline boundaries instead of raw char offsets — prevents cutting mid-entity across chunks - Removed Markdown parse-entity retry logic (was the fallback for v1 failures; no longer needed with HTML mode) - parseMode option updated from 'Markdown' | null to 'HTML' | null - 17 tests updated/added covering conversion, escaping, chunking Fixes #179 Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 * fix(telegram): update OutboundLogMetadata parseMode type to html | none * fix(telegram): remove stale parseFallback refs from logging.ts * feat(telegram): add [text](url) link conversion to markdownToHtml Closes the last Markdown feature gap vs Telegram Markdown v1. Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 --------- Co-authored-by: Boris Co-authored-by: Claude Sonnet 4.6

commits.author: James Goldbach
commits.subject: fix(daemon): extend gap detection to cron-expression crons (#169) (#184)
commits.body:
* fix(daemon): extend gap detection to cron-expression crons (#169)

Crons using a `cron:` expression field (e.g. "3 9 * * *") were silently
excluded from scheduleGapDetection() because the filter only accepted
entries with a parseable `interval:` field. This left ~90% of production
crons — including morning-review, evening-review, and autoresearch — with
no dead-zone coverage.

Changes:
- Add cronExpressionMinIntervalMs() to cron-state.ts: derives a minimum
  expected firing interval from a 5-field cron expression without external
  deps. Handles every-N-minutes, every-N-hours, and daily patterns;
  falls back to a conservative 48h for anything else.
- Extend the monitorable filter in scheduleGapDetection() to include
  crons with a cron: field in addition to interval: crons.
- Update runGapDetectionLoop() to resolve intervalMs from either source.
- Adjust the restore hint in the nudge message for cron-expression crons
  (no /loop interval syntax applies).

Fixes #169.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(daemon): clamp gap detector baseline to loopStartedAt after restart

After a restart storm, cron-state.json retains pre-storm last_fire
timestamps. The gap detector was using those stale values, causing
false-positive nudges every 10 minutes even with crons confirmed
active on every CronList check.

Fix: clamp lastFireMs to max(lastFireMs, loopStartedAt) so that any
recorded fire time older than the current daemon start is treated as
a fresh baseline. Crons that haven't fired since the restart get the
same grace window as crons with no record at all.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

commits.author: James Goldbach
commits.subject: fix(telegram): validate BOT_TOKEN and CHAT_ID against Telegram API before enable + setup writes .env (#235)
commits.body:
Agents could previously boot on silently broken credentials — a bad BOT_TOKEN,
a CHAT_ID that was never opened with /start, a bot-recipient CHAT_ID, or the
self_chat trap where someone pastes the BOT_TOKEN prefix (the bot's own user
id) into CHAT_ID. First contact with Telegram only happened at first real
sendMessage, which failed with a cryptic 401/400/403 buried in the agent's
stdout log while the dashboard kept showing the agent as alive. Observed
in the field: a fresh agent provisioned with CHAT_ID equal to the first
segment of BOT_TOKEN (the bot's own user id) — `sendMessage` returned
403 "bots can't send messages to bots", but nothing else in the system
surfaced the misconfiguration.

Adds TelegramAPI.validateCredentials() — a config-time probe that calls only
getMe and getChat (no sendMessage), returns a tagged discriminated union with
6 failure reasons (bad_token, chat_not_found, bot_recipient, self_chat,
network_error, rate_limited), and a matching formatValidateError() so
enable-agent.ts and setup.ts never diverge on user-facing error text. Never
leaks any portion of BOT_TOKEN into any error message (verified in test).
Each probe call is bounded at 10s via an internal withTimeout helper so a
network partition cannot hang enable or setup indefinitely.

Wires the probe into \`cortextos enable <agent>\` as a preflight right after
the existing BOT_TOKEN/CHAT_ID presence check. network_error and rate_limited
are WARNING-not-fail so offline enable and burst enables during morning
cascade still succeed.

Wires the probe into \`cortextos setup\` (both orchestrator-creation and
additional-agent loop) BEFORE writeAgentEnv(), so a broken .env is never
committed to disk. Gives the user up to 3 recoverable re-entries; bails
entirely on bad_token (requires BotFather fix).

Adds 16 unit tests in tests/unit/telegram/api.test.ts covering every branch
of validateCredentials (including the 10s timeout) and every formatValidateError
message, with explicit regression guards for the self_chat case and the
never-leak-token invariant.

Co-authored-by: ClintMoody <ClintMoody@users.noreply.github.com>

+/**
+ * crons-schema.ts — Path constants and helpers for the external persistent cron system.
+ *
+ * Subtask 1.1 (schema design).  Intentionally thin: only constants and a path
+ * joiner.  Read/write operations live in Subtask 1.2 (src/bus/crons.ts).
+ *
+ * Per-agent crons.json location:
+ *   {CRONS_DIRECTORY}/{agentName}/{CRONS_FILENAME}
+ *   => .cortextOS/state/agents/boris/crons.json
+ */
+
+import { join } from 'path';
+
+/**
+ * Root directory that holds per-agent state sub-directories.
+ * Relative to CTX_ROOT; callers that need an absolute path should
+ * prefix with the CTX_ROOT env var or the framework root from CtxEnv.
+ *
+ * @example ".cortextOS/state/agents"
+ */
+export const CRONS_DIRECTORY = '.cortextOS/state/agents';
+
+/**
+ * File name for the cron definitions list inside each agent state directory.
+ *
+ * @example "crons.json"
+ */
+export const CRONS_FILENAME = 'crons.json';
+
+/**
+ * Return the path to an agent's crons.json relative to CTX_ROOT.
+ *
+ * @param agentName - The agent's directory name (e.g. "boris", "paul").
+ * @returns Relative path string: `.cortextOS/state/agents/{agentName}/crons.json`
+ *
+ * @example
+ * cronsPathFor("boris")
+ * // => ".cortextOS/state/agents/boris/crons.json"
+ */
+export function cronsPathFor(agentName: string): string {
+  return join(CRONS_DIRECTORY, agentName, CRONS_FILENAME);
+}

+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+// External Persistent Cron System — Subtask 1.1
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+//
+// CronDefinition is the canonical record stored in per-agent crons.json files:
+//   .cortextOS/state/agents/{agent_name}/crons.json
+//
+// The file is an array of CronDefinition objects.  The daemon reads it, schedules
+// each enabled cron, and injects the prompt into the agent's PTY on schedule.
+//
+// Operators may edit crons.json by hand (it is intentionally human-readable).
+// Keep all field names lowercase-snake-case and all times as ISO 8601 UTC.
+//
+// Example records
+// ---------------
+//
+// Heartbeat — every 6 hours (interval shorthand):
+// {
+//   "name": "heartbeat",
+//   "schedule": "6h",
+//   "prompt": "Read HEARTBEAT.md and execute the heartbeat workflow.",
+//   "enabled": true,
+//   "created_at": "2026-04-01T00:00:00.000Z",
+//   "description": "Periodic health check and status update."
+// }
+//
+// Daily morning briefing — fixed local time via cron expression:
+// {
+//   "name": "morning-briefing",
+//   "schedule": "0 13 * * *",
+//   "prompt": "Prepare and send the morning briefing to James.",
+//   "enabled": true,
+//   "created_at": "2026-04-01T00:00:00.000Z",
+//   "description": "Daily 09:00 ET briefing (UTC offset applied in schedule).",
+//   "last_fired_at": "2026-04-28T13:00:01.042Z",
+//   "fire_count": 14
+// }
+//
+// Weekly report — cron expression with day-of-week restriction:
+// {
+//   "name": "weekly-report",
+//   "schedule": "0 16 * * 1",
+//   "prompt": "Compile and send the weekly performance report.",
+//   "enabled": true,
+//   "created_at": "2026-04-01T00:00:00.000Z",
+//   "description": "Every Monday at 12:00 ET (16:00 UTC).",
+//   "fire_count": 3
+// }
+
+/**
+ * A single persistent cron definition stored in an agent's crons.json.
+ *
+ * Stored at: `.cortextOS/state/agents/{agent_name}/crons.json`
+ *
+ * The `schedule` field accepts two formats:
+ *   - Interval shorthand: `"6h"`, `"30m"`, `"1d"`, `"2w"`
+ *     Parsed by `parseDurationMs()` from `src/bus/cron-state.ts`.
+ *   - Standard 5-field cron expression: `"0 8 * * *"`, `"0 0,6,12,18 * * *"` (every 6h)
+ *     Evaluated by the daemon scheduler (Subtask 1.3).
+ *
+ * The daemon fires the cron by injecting `[CRON: {name}] {prompt}` into
+ * the agent's PTY session.
+ */
+export interface CronDefinition {
+  // ------------------------------------------------------------------
+  // Required fields — must be present for the daemon to schedule this cron.
+  // ------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+  /**
+   * Unique identifier for this cron within the agent.
+   * Used as the key for lookups, updates, and deletions.
+   * Must be unique per agent; slugs like "heartbeat" or "morning-briefing" are recommended.
+   *
+   * @example "heartbeat"
+   * @example "morning-briefing"
+   */
+  name: string;
+
+  /**
+   * The prompt text injected into the agent PTY when the cron fires.
+   * The daemon prepends `[CRON: {name}] ` automatically for traceability.
+   *
+   * @example "Read HEARTBEAT.md and execute the heartbeat workflow."
+   */
+  prompt: string;
+
+  /**
+   * When and how often this cron fires.
+   *
+   * Accepted formats:
+   *   - Interval shorthand: `"6h"`, `"30m"`, `"1d"`, `"2w"`
+   *     The cron fires every N units after its previous fire (or after daemon start
+   *     if it has never fired).
+   *   - 5-field cron expression: `"0 8 * * *"`, `"0 0,6,12,18 * * *"`, `"0 16 * * 1"`
+   *     Evaluated against the daemon's wall clock (daemon timezone = server timezone).
+   *
+   * @example "6h"         — every six hours
+   * @example "0 13 * * *" — daily at 13:00 UTC
+   * @example "0 16 * * 1" — every Monday at 16:00 UTC
+   */
+  schedule: string;
+
+  /**
+   * Whether the daemon should fire this cron.
+   * Set to `false` to pause a cron without deleting it.
+   *
+   * @default true
+   */
+  enabled: boolean;
+
+  /**
+   * ISO 8601 UTC timestamp of when this cron definition was created.
+   * Set automatically by `cortextos bus add-cron`; operators should not modify this.
+   *
+   * @example "2026-04-01T00:00:00.000Z"
+   */
+  created_at: string;
+
+  // ------------------------------------------------------------------
+  // Optional fields — populated at runtime or by operators.
+  // ------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+  /**
+   * ISO 8601 UTC timestamp of the most recent successful fire.
+   * Updated by the daemon scheduler (Subtask 1.3) after each fire.
+   * Absent when the cron has never fired.
+   *
+   * @example "2026-04-28T13:00:01.042Z"
+   */
+  last_fired_at?: string;
+
+  /**
+   * Total number of times this cron has successfully fired.
+   * Incremented by the daemon on each successful PTY injection.
+   * Absent (or 0) when the cron has never fired.
+   */
+  fire_count?: number;
+
+  /**
+   * Human-readable description of what this cron does.
+   * Optional — for operator documentation and dashboard display.
+   *
+   * @example "Periodic health check and status update."
+   */
+  description?: string;
+
+  /**
+   * Arbitrary key-value pairs for agent-specific context.
+   * Not interpreted by the daemon; surfaced in dashboard + execution logs.
+   *
+   * @example { "priority": "high", "source": "/loop" }
+   */
+  metadata?: Record<string, unknown>;
+}
+
 export interface OrgContext {
   name?: string;
   description?: string;

+import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
+import { join } from 'path';
+import {
+  CRONS_DIRECTORY,
+  CRONS_FILENAME,
+  cronsPathFor,
+} from '../../../src/bus/crons-schema';
+import type { CronDefinition } from '../../../src/types/index';
+
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+// cronsPathFor — path helper
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+describe('cronsPathFor', () => {
+  it('returns the expected path for agent "boris"', () => {
+    const expected = join('.cortextOS', 'state', 'agents', 'boris', 'crons.json');
+    expect(cronsPathFor('boris')).toBe(expected);
+  });
+
+  it('uses CRONS_DIRECTORY and CRONS_FILENAME constants', () => {
+    const result = cronsPathFor('paul');
+    expect(result).toContain(CRONS_DIRECTORY.replace(/\//g, join('/')));
+    expect(result.endsWith(CRONS_FILENAME)).toBe(true);
+  });
+
+  it('is consistent for any agent name', () => {
+    expect(cronsPathFor('sentinel')).toBe(
+      join(CRONS_DIRECTORY, 'sentinel', CRONS_FILENAME)
+    );
+  });
+
+  it('handles agent names with hyphens', () => {
+    expect(cronsPathFor('data-agent')).toBe(
+      join(CRONS_DIRECTORY, 'data-agent', CRONS_FILENAME)
+    );
+  });
+});
+
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+// CronDefinition compile-time shape test
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+//
+// These objects are declared as CronDefinition — if any required field is
+// absent or has the wrong type, TypeScript will flag a compile error.
+// The tests just confirm the objects are accepted by the type system and
+// have the expected runtime values.
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+describe('CronDefinition — type shape', () => {
+  it('accepts a minimal required-fields-only definition', () => {
+    const heartbeat: CronDefinition = {
+      name: 'heartbeat',
+      prompt: 'Read HEARTBEAT.md and execute the heartbeat workflow.',
+      schedule: '6h',
+      enabled: true,
+      created_at: '2026-04-01T00:00:00.000Z',
+    };
+
+    expect(heartbeat.name).toBe('heartbeat');
+    expect(heartbeat.schedule).toBe('6h');
+    expect(heartbeat.enabled).toBe(true);
+    expect(heartbeat.last_fired_at).toBeUndefined();
+    expect(heartbeat.fire_count).toBeUndefined();
+  });
+
+  it('accepts a full definition with all optional fields', () => {
+    const briefing: CronDefinition = {
+      name: 'morning-briefing',
+      prompt: 'Prepare and send the morning briefing to James.',
+      schedule: '0 13 * * *',
+      enabled: true,
+      created_at: '2026-04-01T00:00:00.000Z',
+      description: 'Daily 09:00 ET briefing (UTC offset applied in schedule).',
+      last_fired_at: '2026-04-28T13:00:01.042Z',
+      fire_count: 14,
+      metadata: { priority: 'high', source: '/loop' },
+    };
+
+    expect(briefing.name).toBe('morning-briefing');
+    expect(briefing.schedule).toBe('0 13 * * *');
+    expect(briefing.fire_count).toBe(14);
+    expect(briefing.last_fired_at).toBe('2026-04-28T13:00:01.042Z');
+    expect(briefing.metadata?.['source']).toBe('/loop');
+  });
+
+  it('accepts a weekly cron with day-of-week expression', () => {
+    const weekly: CronDefinition = {
+      name: 'weekly-report',
+      prompt: 'Compile and send the weekly performance report.',
+      schedule: '0 16 * * 1',
+      enabled: true,
+      created_at: '2026-04-01T00:00:00.000Z',
+      description: 'Every Monday at 12:00 ET (16:00 UTC).',
+      fire_count: 3,
+    };
+
+    expect(weekly.name).toBe('weekly-report');
+    expect(weekly.schedule).toBe('0 16 * * 1');
+    expect(weekly.enabled).toBe(true);
+  });
+
+  it('accepts enabled: false (disabled cron)', () => {
+    const paused: CronDefinition = {
+      name: 'paused-task',
+      prompt: 'This cron is temporarily disabled.',
+      schedule: '30m',
+      enabled: false,
+      created_at: '2026-04-01T00:00:00.000Z',
+    };
+
+    expect(paused.enabled).toBe(false);
+  });
+});
